title: Give a newborn manikin five inflation breaths with an infant bag and mask
instruction: Give the newborn manikin five inflation breaths of 2 to 3 s each with the bag and mask from the tray, so that its chest rises with every breath. Do not press on its eyes. Finish with the mask still held on the face and the bag let go.
context: A newborn who does not breathe after drying and stimulation is given five inflation breaths of 2 to 3 s through a face mask on a self-inflating bag, watching for the chest to rise: the first step of newborn life support. Each year about 10 million babies need help to start breathing and about 6 million need basic resuscitation, usually with bag and mask, many where skilled hands are few (Wall et al. 2009). It takes two hands: one presses the round mask evenly on the face over nose and mouth, the other squeezes the bag. A light hold leaks, so the chest does not rise; a crushing hold shuts the airway; a push on the bag, which hangs off the valve to one side, tips the mask; a mask on the eyes can hurt. Midwives, nurses and paramedics train and retrain this act on exactly such a manikin; a robot assistant at a birth, or a trainer, would need it.
setup: Bimanual YAM station. Millimetres; x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top; arm bases at y +305 and -305. (1) A newborn training manikin whose chest rises only when breaths go in through a sealed mask (the Laerdal NeoNatalie, from 85 USD, is the low-cost route; published). It lies on its back on the midline along x, crown toward the robot, its body fixed to the table, its head on a flat digital kitchen scale (1 g steps, zeroed with the head on) let into the table so the face is at the height below. Estimates (est): crown at x 164, chin at x 289; the mask's target point (midway between nose tip and chin) at x 250 mm, y 0, the face round it 90 mm over the table; eyes centred at x 206, y +-21, z 82; chest top at x 365, z 104. (2) An infant self-inflating bag with a 280 mL bag, a 40 cmH2O relief valve and a 360 degree swivel at the mask (Intersurgical 7150000; published), with a Laerdal Newborn Mask size 1 (round silicone, 64 mm across, 37 g; published) on the swivel. Estimates (est): bag 150 mm long, 56 mm across; valve housing 56 mm long, its axis 29 mm over the cushion; mask 20 mm tall; the bag joins the valve by a soft neck that bends about +-0.5 rad; whole assembly 147 g. (3) A tray 96 x 290 x 10 mm fixed in front of the crown (x 62 to 158, y -245 to 45). The bag and mask lie on it mask down, the mask's axis at x 110, y 0, the bag level toward -y, in a painted outline. Nothing else on the table. (4) Acceptance checks before the first trial (spring scale, ruler): with the mask held on the face at 2 to 10 N, squeezing the bag 10 mm across its middle and holding it 2 s raises the chest 4 to 9 mm (rise read against a 1 mm scale); with the mask resting under its own weight the same squeeze raises it under 1 mm; squeezing the bag 10 mm takes under 5 N; the swivel turns freely. Parts that fail are not used.
scoring: Read every step from the poses of the bag and mask, its joints and the grippers. Sealed: the mask's axis within 8 mm (top view) of the target point, tilted 6 degrees or less, the cushion touching the face (its lower face 0.5 mm or less over it), every part of the cushion pressed 0.3 mm or more and none at its 10 mm stop, and the cushion's force 2 to 10 N (over 10 N presses the airway shut). Kinked: the bag's neck bent over 0.40 rad. Squeeze: how far the bag is pressed in across its middle. Rise (declared air rule): while sealed and not kinked, every further mm of squeeze raises the chest 0.6 mm; easing the squeeze 1 mm off its peak lets the chest fall (time constant 0.3 s); unsealed or kinked, the chest falls (0.2 s) and squeezing does nothing; capped at 12 mm. Inflation: the rise at 4 mm or more (dips that stay over 1 mm join), counted when it falls under 1 mm; good if it lasted 2.0 to 3.0 s. Latched: too long, any inflation over 3.0 s; over-inflated, a rise over 9 mm; dropped, after the mask has been lifted 10 mm off the tray, any part of the bag and mask within 2 mm of the table; eyes, the bag and mask within 1 mm, or a gripper's fingers within 2 mm, of an eye zone (a 7.5 mm ball round each eye); lifted, after the first good inflation, unsealed for over 1.0 s at a time. At rest: on every step of the last 1.0 s, sealed, squeeze under 2 mm, every finger 5 mm or more from the bag, rise under 1 mm. Score 0 if eyes, or no good inflation; else 0.25 if over-inflated or dropped; else 0.5 if too long; else 1.0 for exactly 5 inflations, all good, at rest and never lifted; 0.75 for 5 or more good otherwise; 0.5 for 3 or 4; 0.25 for 1 or 2. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held 1 s. Real trial, same manikin and bag, room air: rise from 30 fps side video against a 1 mm scale beside the chest marked at 1, 4 and 9 mm, read frame by frame (an inflation's length from its frame count); sealed, at every frame from the first good inflation on (between breaths and at rest too): the head's scale, filmed beside the face, reads 204 to 1020 g (2 to 10 N) over the head's own weight and the top video shows the cushion's rim on the face all round, its centre within 8 mm of the marked target point; a leak while squeezing also shows as no rise; eyes from the cushion rim chalked before the trial (chalk on an eye counts) and top video for any finger at an eye; dropped, lifted and at rest from the videos, the target point marked on the face. Tries are not penalised.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; the face is a rigid level seat and the head is fixed (its scale is not modelled). The cushion is 8 pads on sprung slides (150 N/m each, 10 mm travel, est); the bag is a rigid ellipsoid with two squeeze panels on sprung slides (400 N/m each, est), on a free neck hinge (+-0.5 rad) and a free swivel. Air is the declared rule in scoring: the seal is read from the pads and the chest plate is driven to the rise. No air flow, leak or lung is simulated.
reset_notes: Lift the mask straight off the face and lay the bag and mask back in the tray's painted outline, mask down, bag level toward -y. Let the manikin's chest fall and the bag spring back to round. Wipe any chalk off the eyes and re-chalk the cushion rim. Nothing is consumed; between trials check that the swivel turns freely.
